name: Snaketown Hohokam canal irrigation
description: Archaeological reconstruction identifies a Snaketown-area Hohokam irrigation canal in the Middle Gila River valley during the Early Pioneer period.

date.label: 450–650 CE, archaeological period
date.basis: Date concerns this identified object, archaeological phase or documentary observation; it does not assert a global origin.

events.statement: Archaeological reconstruction identifies a Snaketown-area Hohokam irrigation canal in the Middle Gila River valley during the Early Pioneer period.

evidence.locator: Case selection, canal development, methods and conclusions
evidence.supports: The authors reconstruct Snaketown-area canal expansion using Woodson’s period chronology, describing a canal in 450–650 CE and enlargement during 750–850 CE. Hydraulic outcomes are model estimates based on assumptions, not observed ancient flows; coordination arrangements remain uncertain.

events.caveats: The date is a period-level archaeological reconstruction, not direct dating of every canal section or a claim of the origin of American irrigation. Water allocation rules and the identities of individual builders are not established.
